horizontal.escena:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: one independent image in a three-part editorial paper-cut story illustration for a Colombian folktale.
Source boundary: illustrate the existing published adaptation of the story of Nephew Rabbit and Uncle Tigre. Community attribution remains unconfirmed; the source catalogue only locates the title under Eastern Plains and Amazonia. These are editorial fictional animal designs. There are no people, traditional costumes, sacred symbols or claimed Indigenous practices. In our artwork Tigre is a spotted jaguar as an explicitly declared editorial choice, not a taxonomic assertion from the book. Do not add a date or archaeological claims.
Medium: a remarkably expressive flat illustrated WORLD OF CUT PAPER, full bleed to every edge. Thick matte dyed cardstock, plainly visible cream cut cross-sections, lifted irregular cut edges, curled leaf tips, central folded leaf veins, separate cut rosettes on the jaguar, layered paper fur shapes, and strongly legible soft contact shadows between separated planes. Every tiny form should read as hand-cut paper even at thumbnail size. Botanical foreground, middle scene, and low tropical canopy fade through separate stacked silhouettes. No plastic, sculpted doll faces, CGI, polished diorama plinth, painted/photographic fur, spectacle of faceting, labels or typography.
Character consistency: exactly one small russet-brown Rabbit, long upright or swept-back ears with muted terracotta inner paper, cream chin and small cream tail, thoughtful dark eyes, compact believable animal body and four anatomically coherent limbs. No clothing or human hands. Exactly one Uncle Tigre when the scene requests him: a low massive ochre-gold spotted JAGUAR, black rosettes, cream muzzle, rounded ears, four powerful paws, long thick ringed tail. His expression comes from quiet paper-eye and ear planes, no exaggerated teeth or monster anatomy.
All principal subjects including ear tips, every paw, snout and tail tip must remain fully within the image, at least 10 percent from every edge. Frame the story in a generous environment rather than cutting a portrait. No border or captions, logos, watermark, letters or speech bubbles.
Primary request: create ENTRADA, a spacious horizontal 16:9 composition. Reference 1 supplies the cut-paper jaguar construction and the shallow warm low-canopy tropical world; reference 2 supplies leaf folds, canopy depth and matte paper. Draw an entirely new scene. Do NOT copy the lizard, the hollow tree, either reflected sun, puddle or two-jaguar arrangement from reference 1.
Scene: a small watermelon patch at the tropical forest edge in warm late afternoon. Whole russet Rabbit at center-left has just struck a sticky trap and both forepaws are attached to a SMALL plain amber-ochre resin figure. His two hindfeet brace on the ground; both ears and his entire cream tail are visible. This is comic frustration and an immobilized animal, not mutilation or a fight. The trap is an unpainted rounded branch-like dummy with a blank oval head and no facial features or cultural ornament. Its stickiness is conveyed through a few cut translucent-looking warm PAPER bridges at paw contact, not drooling liquid. Two whole green striped watermelons lie among folded vine leaves beside it. Do not invent farm tools, fences, modern homes or chemical bottles.
Farther behind, a SINGLE whole ochre jaguar approaches along the low forest path, all four paws and tail tip clearly inside the wide frame. He is smaller through real pictorial distance, not a second close portrait. Rabbit, trap and fruit are the focal cluster; jaguar shows the adversary discovering the trap. Preserve clear open separation between subjects. Use burnt ochre, russet, muted melon-red accents and olive foliage. Everything is cut cardstock. The leaf foreground may meet the border; neither animal may do so.

vertical.escena:
Edit reference 1, preserving its vertical 9:16 paper-cut medium and the two fictional animal identities, also shown in reference 2. Correct the scene construction. This is an independent illustration of the existing public adaptation of Nephew Rabbit and Uncle Tigre; community attribution is unconfirmed. No humans or claimed traditional symbols.
CRITICAL correction 1: the cave must be a real connected low-forest ROCK OPENING planted in the continuous ground, not a floating slab, elevated island or hanging paper stage. Rebuild the layout: the entire upper-left half is continuous stacked dark teal and indigo rock with an opening inside it. Rabbit crouches WHOLE inside this opening, at roughly x=35 percent, y=45 percent, on an earth floor. That same earth floor extends in a gently descending DIAGONAL unbroken visible path toward the lower-right through foliage, where the WHOLE jaguar retreats, at roughly x=60 percent, y=70 percent. No open-air canopy or window UNDER the cave floor. The earth path connects the cave to the jaguar's four paws; shadows agree with one grounded scene. Background tropical leaves beyond the descending path, not underneath a floating rock. The top foliage canopy and bottom foreground may reach the image edges. Leave generous breathing room, animals around one fifth to one quarter of image height; no paws, ears or tail tips within the outer 10 percent of the frame.
CRITICAL correction 2: REMOVE all four perfect crescent/Wi-Fi/loudspeaker icon shapes. Show the little Rabbit's large voice as only two long irregular ochre paper strips with uneven hand-cut contours and small lifted folds. These leave the mouth gently, curl loosely through the opening into the air and taper outward. They have NO regular repeated radius, NO diagram, NO perfect parallel crescent, NO letters, symbols, arrows or text. They are an editorial visualization of sound, not a real monster or animal. Rabbit mouth is visibly open as speaker; jaguar recoils, looking back without seeing Rabbit. Do not add any third creature or giant shadow monster.
Keep Rabbit russet brown, cream chin and tail, long terracotta inner ears, coherent four limbs. Keep a single jaguar ochre, black paper rosettes, cream muzzle, round ears, quiet expressive eyes, four powerful paws and whole ringed tail. All main body parts completely inside frame, naturally overlapping limbs allowed but no broken anatomy or arbitrary appendages. No rabbit clothes or human hands, no jaguar teeth spectacle.
Strongly expressive hand-cut MATTE THICK PAPER everywhere: cream cut cross-sections, staggered rock cut edges, separate lifted rosettes, irregular layered fur, folded leaf veins, curled leaf tips and clear soft contact shadows between all paper planes. Flat illustrated depth, not plastic or polished 3D sculpture. Cooler indigo/teal cave, pale gold light at its actual grounded mouth, jade humid foliage below, warm earth path. No typography, captions, border, plinth or watermark. New corrected image, leave prior original untouched.

Primary request: create HUELLA, a SQUARE 1:1 symbolic editorial image with ONE unified motif and ONE paper operation. It is a newly authored metaphor for a small character finding a way out of a stronger adversary's power; it is NOT a literal episode or a certified traditional symbol.
ONE motif: a single complete giant stylized JAGUAR PAWPRINT made from stacked midnight-blue and charcoal matte cardstock on a quiet terracotta and ochre forest-floor paper background. It consists of exactly four rounded toe pads above one broad central palm pad, arranged as one unmistakable FELINE pawprint. No human fingers, no fifth toe, no literal jaguar, no human, no trap, no watermelon, no separate real rabbit.
ONE operation: a small integral flap in the CENTRAL palm pad is folded and lifted outward. The opening it reveals is a whole clear RABBIT-SHAPED NEGATIVE SPACE, with two long ears, a small snout, compact body, coherent little legs and tail, all visible. Through that opening a pale gold lower paper layer appears as a narrow passage into olive foliage: the smaller silhouette has made an exit through the larger mark. The Rabbit-shaped opening is noticeably smaller than the pawprint, and is a hole in it, not a pasted animal sitting on top. One clean folded lip makes the opening physically legible. Abstract and poetic, without words or a symbol legend.
Use reference 1 only for Rabbit outline proportions, handmade paper treatment, cut rosette edge thickness and leaf folds. Do NOT reproduce either animal as an actual character or its scene. Reference 2 only supplies discreet leaf-paper texture. Pawprint is entire and centered with all pad tips at least 12 percent from every edge. Foliage and scattered low leaf silhouettes stay subtle around the periphery and reach the frame, no border or empty backdrop. Thick cream cut edges, offset paper layers and strongly visible soft contact shadows. Make the fold and negative space readable at thumbnail size. Restrained indigo, warm copper, gold paper and olive; matte, no liquid shine or CGI.
